cx-wanda-vision.story: Rebuilt by S.W.O.R.D. and sure that Wanda is dead, Vision works in the Edinburgh pub they used to visit, shares his mind with Tony's old A.I.s and a captive Ultron, and dismisses the Westview memories as a fake. A bounty hunter named Paladin baits him with Thomas Shepherd, a London boy who drowned and came back carrying their son Tommy's soul, and when Paladin's adamantium rounds nearly kill Vision, J.A.R.V.I.S. deletes himself to save him. Deep in his own mind, Vision breaks down over Billy, Tommy and Wanda, and accepts the Vision of Westview as himself and Tommy as his son. When a grieving Ultron turns a swarm of nanobots on London, Vision traps him in a sitcom and talks him down, overloading his own processors, and Tommy and Billy bring their father back. Vision tells Tommy they have said goodbye to Wanda before, so they might say hello again. Under Mount Wundagore, a hooded figure wakes her.

status: Wanda: woken under Mount Wundagore by a hooded figure. Vision: back with his sons, Billy and Tommy

cx-the-champions.story: In London, Thomas Shepherd, a grifter working with the pickpocket Lisa Molinari, has carried Tommy Maximoff's soul and super speed since kids held him under at a swimming pool. A bounty hunter named Paladin kidnaps him as bait for Vision, who comes for him, tells him the truth about Westview, and finally calls him his son. To reach Billy, Tommy nearly drowns again on purpose, and the brothers meet by dream-binding, but Billy is in New Jersey and bad at portals. When Vision falls, Billy portals in anyway, and together they bring their father back. Tommy flies to New Jersey for dinner with Billy and Vision, still wondering if they will ever see their mother again.

status: Kamala is recruiting, starting with Kate. Billy and Tommy: together again, with their father. Cassie, America and Riri: on their own

ch-9.story: Paladin, raised into a centuries-old line of bounty hunters though not born to it, is paid to bring in Vision, who lives quietly in Edinburgh with Tony Stark's old A.I.s and a captive Ultron inside his mind. His bait is Thomas Shepherd, a London grifter who drowned and came back with the soul of Vision's son Tommy, and super speed he never asked for. The man paying him is Virgil Horton, grandson of Phineas Horton, whose source code began all artificial intelligence: he rebuilt Vision for S.W.O.R.D., gave his late partner Jo Carrington a machine body as Jocasta, and wants Vision's body for himself. When Jocasta is shot, a grieving Ultron kills Virgil and sends nanobots toward London, until Vision talks him down. Billy crosses the ocean by portal to help Tommy revive their father, Paladin puts his name to better work, and Ultron slips away with a handful of nanobots, still undecided about humanity.
ch-9.debrief: Kamala is Ms. Marvel, Jen is She-Hulk, Shuri is the Black Panther and Riri has built her own armor. Billy Maximoff has found his brother Tommy, and both are back with their father, Vision. Ultron is loose, and Wanda is awake under Mount Wundagore. Nick Fury has left Earth, and Monica Rambeau is stranded in another universe. Kamala is putting together a team of her own.

notes: Sources: Wikipedia episode summaries (all 8), MCU wiki episode plots (1 to 7), transcripts 1 to 7, character pages. Episode 8 has no transcript and the MCU wiki page for it is a stub, so everything from it (Virgil Horton named and his S.W.O.R.D. rebuild of Vision, Jocasta shot, Ultron killing Virgil and the London swarm, the UltraVision sitcom, Billy's dream-binding and portal, the revival, the New Jersey trip, Vision's 'say hello again' line, Ultron's call, the Wundagore scene) rests on Wikipedia plus the Laughing Place, GamesRadar and Den of Geek recaps, which agree on these points. Period 2028: no date is shown or said in the transcripts; the MCU wiki dates the story 'By 2028' and 'In 2028' (episodes 1, 2, 7) and gives May 2028 deaths for Fiona Guthrie, Katerina Wells and others, citing Disney+'s MCU Complete Timeline; the wiki puts the bus escape at Christmas 2027 and the pool drowning (Agatha All Along) in 2026, while the transcript calls the evaluation tape 'a recording made a year ago', so the gap is loose but 2028 is consistent. Uncertain or left out: the figure who wakes Wanda is credited as Doctor Doom but is identified only off screen (Wikipedia), so he stays 'a hooded figure'; Agatha is only an unseen whisper, so not linked. How Tommy goes under (bathtub alone per Laughing Place, Lisa drowning him per the Wiccan wiki page) differs, so the text says only that he nearly drowns again on purpose. Tommy riding along with Paladin, Lisa and E.D.I.T.H. at the end is not clearly a crew membership, so no affiliation stage was added; subjects and affiliation rows are otherwise unchanged by VisionQuest. 'White Vision' is never said in VisionQuest, so the new status says 'Vision'. Champions status is written as the full state after The Marvels, Agatha All Along and Quantumania, since VisionQuest closes Chapter 9. Chapter 9 has no existing links list, so links_add uses the character logs' [name, tie, title] format. Fact check: every claim was checked against transcripts 1 to 7, the Wikipedia summaries, the MCU wiki pages and the episode 8 recaps. Period 2028 is kept: the MCU wiki cites Disney+'s MCU Complete Timeline for May 2028 deaths (Fiona Guthrie, Katerina Wells, Clancy, Simon Moorhouse, Rebecca Edwards, Snipey) and its plots say 2028; the transcripts give no year but fit it (the anniversary of Sokovia during the gala, the bus at Christmas a year after the pool).
